questions.prompt: In Kepler's ellipse model, is the central mass at the center of the ellipse or at one focus?
questions.answer: The central mass is at one focus of the ellipse, not at the geometric center.

questions.prompt: An orbiting body sweeps equal areas in equal times. Is it moving faster near periapsis or apoapsis?
questions.answer: It moves faster near periapsis. When \(r\) is smaller, a larger transverse speed is needed to sweep the same area in the same time.

questions.prompt: Two objects orbit the same star. One has semi-major axis \(4a\), and the other has semi-major axis \(a\). Find the ratio of their periods.
questions.answer:
For the same central mass,
\[
T\propto a^{3/2}
\]
so
\[
\frac{T_{4a}}{T_a}=4^{3/2}=8
\]

questions.prompt: An elliptical orbit has periapsis distance \(7.0\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{m}\) and apoapsis distance \(1.9\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{m}\). Find its semi-major axis.
Find the period of an orbit with \(a=1.5\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{m}\) around a star of mass \(2.0\times10^{30}\,\mathrm{kg}\). Use \(G=6.67\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{N\,m^2\,kg^{-2}}\).
An object orbits with semi-major axis \(2.0\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{m}\) and period \(5.0\times10^7\,\mathrm{s}\). Estimate the central mass.
questions.answer:
From Kepler's third law,
\[
T^2=\frac{4\pi^2}{GM}a^3
\]
so
\[
M=\frac{4\pi^2a^3}{GT^2}
\]
\[
M=\frac{4\pi^2(2.0\times10^{11})^3}{(6.67\times10^{-11})(5.0\times10^7)^2}
=1.9\times10^{30}\,\mathrm{kg}
\]

questions.prompt: At periapsis \(r_p=4.0\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{m}\), and at apoapsis \(r_a=1.2\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{m}\). Use angular momentum conservation to find \(v_p/v_a\).
questions.answer:
At apsides the velocity is transverse, so angular momentum conservation gives
\[
mr_pv_p=mr_av_a
\]
Therefore
\[
\frac{v_p}{v_a}=\frac{r_a}{r_p}
=\frac{1.2\times10^{11}}{4.0\times10^{10}}
=3
\]
The object is three times faster at periapsis.

questions.prompt: Two planets have the same semi-major axis, but one orbits a star with four times the mass of the other star. Compare their orbital periods.
questions.answer:
For fixed \(a\),
\[
T=2\pi\sqrt{\frac{a^3}{GM}}\propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{M}}
\]
If the central mass is four times larger,
\[
T_{\mathrm{large}\,M}=\frac{1}{2}T_{\mathrm{small}\,M}
\]
The orbit around the more massive star has half the period.

questions.prompt: An elliptical orbit around a fixed star has \(r_p=1.0\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{m}\) and \(r_a=3.0\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{m}\). Compare its period with a circular orbit of radius \(1.0\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{m}\) around the same star.

For an elliptical orbit with periapsis \(r_p\) and apoapsis \(r_a\), derive the period in terms of \(r_p\), \(r_a\), \(G\), and \(M\). Also derive \(v_p/v_a\), assuming the velocity is perpendicular to the radius at both apsides.
questions.answer:
Ellipse geometry gives
\[
a=\frac{r_p+r_a}{2}
\]
Kepler's third law then gives
\[
T=2\pi\sqrt{\frac{a^3}{GM}}
=2\pi\sqrt{\frac{\left(\frac{r_p+r_a}{2}\right)^3}{GM}}
\]
At periapsis and apoapsis, velocity is perpendicular to the radius, so angular momentum conservation gives
\[
mr_pv_p=mr_av_a
\]
Therefore
\[
\frac{v_p}{v_a}=\frac{r_a}{r_p}
\]
The body moves faster at periapsis because it is closer to the central mass and must sweep equal areas in equal times.
